items.title: Medicaid managed care denies prior authorizations at higher rate than Medicare Advantage: analysis - McKnight's Long-Term Care News
items.reason: This item reports on payer enforcement of prior authorization denial practices—a claims-denial pattern relevant to payer litigation and regulatory scrutiny, though it appears to be an analysis rather than a specific lawsuit or enforcement action.
items.summary: An analysis by McKnight's Long-Term Care News found that Medicaid managed care plans deny prior authorization requests at significantly higher rates than Medicare Advantage plans. The study highlights differential claims-denial practices between these two payer categories, with managed Medicaid showing more restrictive authorization patterns. This disparity in denial rates is relevant to revenue-cycle teams because prior authorization denials directly impact claim submission, appeal costs, and provider cash flow, and may trigger regulatory scrutiny or enforcement actions against payers with outlier denial patterns. The finding underscores the operational and financial exposure healthcare providers face when working with Medicaid managed care versus Medicare Advantage plans.
